events.title: Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker premieres
events.summary: The ballet is first performed at the Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg.
events.description: On December 18, 1892, Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker was first presented at the Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg, Russia.
events.notificationBody: In 1892, Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker premiered in St. Petersburg.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: The Thirteenth Amendment abolishes slavery in the US
events.summary: The constitutional amendment officially enters into force.
events.description: On December 18, 1865, the Thirteenth Amendment to the US Constitution officially entered into force, abolishing slavery in the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: The Piltdown Man is announced
events.summary: A supposed 'missing link' fossil later proves to be a fraud.
events.description: On December 18, 1912, a British Museum paleontologist announced the discovery in England of fossil remains said to be an extinct human species. Presented as a missing link between apes and early humans, the Piltdown Man was exposed as a fraud by the 1950s.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: Antonio Stradivari dies in Cremona
events.summary: The famed Italian violin maker dies.
events.description: On December 18, 1737, the famed Italian violin maker Antonio Stradivari died in Cremona.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 18

events.title: Charles Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol
events.summary: Scrooge's story of redemption becomes an instant classic.
events.description: On December 19, 1843, Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol was published for the first time. Its story of Ebenezer Scrooge's redemption became an instant classic and is still retold on stage and screen.
events.notificationTitle: Bah, humbug, and a classic is born
events.notificationBody: In 1843, Charles Dickens published A Christmas Carol.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: Washington's army goes into winter quarters at Valley Forge
events.summary: About 11,000 Continental troops camp near British-occupied Philadelphia.
events.description: On December 19, 1777, during the American Revolution, General George Washington led 11,000 regulars into winter quarters at Valley Forge, on the Schuylkill River near British-occupied Philadelphia.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: Edith Piaf is born in Paris
events.summary: The singer who made the French chanson world famous is born.
events.description: On December 19, 1915, the singer and actress Edith Piaf, whose interpretation of the French chanson made her internationally famous, was born in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: South Korea elects its first woman president
events.summary: Park Geun-hye wins the presidential election.
events.description: On December 19, 2012, Park Geun-hye was elected the first female president of South Korea. She later became the country's first democratically elected president to be removed from office, after her impeachment in 2017.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 19

events.title: The Brothers Grimm publish their first volume of tales
events.summary: Stories like Hansel and Gretel and Snow White reach print.
events.description: On December 20, 1812, the brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm published the first volume of the stories that made them famous. Their collection, known as Grimm's Fairy Tales, includes 'Hansel and Gretel', 'Snow White', 'Little Red Riding Hood', and 'Sleeping Beauty'.
events.notificationTitle: Once upon a time, in print
events.notificationBody: In 1812, the Brothers Grimm published their first volume of fairy tales.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: Macau returns to Chinese sovereignty
events.summary: Centuries of Portuguese rule come to an end.
events.description: On December 20, 1999, centuries of Portuguese rule in Macau ended when it became a special administrative region under Chinese sovereignty, 12 years after China and Portugal agreed on its status.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: It's a Wonderful Life premieres
events.summary: Frank Capra's drama becomes a holiday classic.
events.description: On December 20, 1946, Frank Capra's It's a Wonderful Life, starring Jimmy Stewart, premiered. It later became a holiday classic.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: South Carolina secedes from the Union
events.summary: The first state to leave follows Lincoln's election.
events.description: On December 20, 1860, following Abraham Lincoln's election as president, South Carolina became the first US state to secede from the Union.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 20

events.title: The first game of basketball is played
events.summary: James Naismith's new game debuts in a Springfield school gym.
events.description: On December 21, 1891, the first game of basketball, organized by gym teacher James Naismith, was played at a school in Springfield, Massachusetts. The chaotic game prompted Naismith to develop the sport's original rules.
events.notificationBody: In 1891, the first game of basketball was played in Springfield.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

events.title: Apollo 8 launches toward the Moon
events.summary: The mission will complete ten lunar orbits.
events.description: On December 21, 1968, Apollo 8 was launched from Cape Kennedy and went on to complete 10 orbits of the Moon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

events.title: Marie and Pierre Curie discover radium
events.summary: The radioactive element is later used in early cancer treatment.
events.description: On December 21, 1898, Marie and Pierre Curie discovered the radioactive element radium, a silvery white metal later used in early cancer treatment.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

events.title: The first modern crossword puzzle is published
events.summary: The New York World introduces a new kind of word game.
events.description: On December 21, 1913, the New York World published the first modern crossword puzzle.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 21

events.title: The Brandenburg Gate reopens
events.summary: Berliners pass through the gate for the first time since 1961.
events.description: On December 22, 1989, the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin reopened as East and West Germany moved toward reunification. Berliners had been unable to use the gate since the Berlin Wall blocked it in 1961.
events.notificationBody: In 1989, Berlin's Brandenburg Gate reopened after 28 years.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: Srinivasa Ramanujan is born
events.summary: The self-taught Indian mathematician is born in Erode.
events.description: On December 22, 1887, Srinivasa Ramanujan, a self-taught Indian mathematician who made many pioneering discoveries, was born in Erode in present-day Tamil Nadu.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: The pope sanctions the Dominican order
events.summary: Honorius III approves the Order of Preachers.
events.description: On December 22, 1216, the Dominican order was sanctioned by Pope Honorius III.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: Leo the Deacon records the solar corona during an eclipse
events.summary: Leo the Deacon's account is the earliest datable description of the corona.
events.description: On December 22, 968, an eclipse of the Sun occurred, and Leo the Deacon described a feeble glow, like a narrow headband, around the darkened Sun: the earliest account of the solar corona that can be linked to a datable eclipse.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 22

events.title: George Washington resigns as commander in chief
events.summary: The victorious general returns his commission to Congress.
events.description: On December 23, 1783, before the Continental Congress, George Washington resigned as commander in chief of the Continental Army.
events.notificationTitle: The general who gave back his power
events.notificationBody: In 1783, George Washington resigned as commander in chief.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: The Ottoman Empire's first constitution takes effect
events.summary: The document gives the sultan full executive power.
events.description: On December 23, 1876, the first comprehensive constitution of the Ottoman Empire went into effect, giving the sultan full executive power.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: The Federal Reserve System is created
events.summary: President Wilson signs the Federal Reserve Act.
events.description: On December 23, 1913, President Woodrow Wilson signed the Federal Reserve Act, bringing the Federal Reserve System into being.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: Jean-Francois Champollion is born
events.summary: The French linguist and historian is born.
events.description: On December 23, 1790, the French historian and linguist Jean-Francois Champollion was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 23

events.title: Edison applies to patent the phonograph
events.summary: The 'speaking machine' is filed with the US Patent Office.
events.description: On December 24, 1877, the US Patent Office received Thomas Edison's application for a 'Phonograph or Speaking Machine'. He had first demonstrated the device weeks earlier by playing back his recorded voice.
events.notificationBody: In 1877, Thomas Edison applied to patent the phonograph.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

events.title: The Treaty of Ghent ends the War of 1812
events.summary: The United States and Britain make peace in Belgium.
events.description: On December 24, 1814, the United States and Great Britain signed the Treaty of Ghent in Belgium, ending the War of 1812.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

events.title: Libya becomes independent under King Idris I
events.summary: The new North African kingdom crowns its first monarch.
events.description: On December 24, 1951, Idris I became the first king of newly independent Libya.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

events.title: King John of England is born
events.summary: The king who sealed Magna Carta is born.
events.description: On December 24, 1167, the future King John of England was born. He lost Normandy and most of his French lands and was forced by rebellious barons to seal Magna Carta in 1215.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 24

events.title: The James Webb Space Telescope launches
events.summary: Hubble's successor lifts off on Christmas Day.
events.description: On December 25, 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope, designed and built by US, Canadian, and European space agencies as the successor to the Hubble Space Telescope, was launched into space.
events.notificationBody: On Christmas Day 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope launched.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
events.summary: The king of the Franks becomes the first emperor of the Holy Roman Empire.
events.description: On December 25, 800, Charlemagne, king of the Franks, became the first emperor of what became the Holy Roman Empire.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: William the Conqueror is crowned king of England
events.summary: The coronation completes the Norman Conquest.
events.description: On December 25, 1066, William I was crowned king of England, formally completing the Norman Conquest.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Washington crosses the Delaware
events.summary: A Christmas night crossing leads to a surprise attack at Trenton.
events.description: On December 25, 1776, during the American Revolution, General George Washington crossed the Delaware River and surprised the British at Trenton, New Jersey.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25

events.title: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president
events.summary: The Soviet Union ceases to exist at the end of the year.
events.description: On December 25, 1991, Mikhail Gorbachev resigned the presidency of the Soviet Union, which ceased to exist at the end of the year.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: December 25
